title: Al-Muntaqim, the Requiter
hookLine: the Requiter, who makes right every wrong
tomorrow: forgive, or erase? why one night's prayer asks for the second.

cards: Somewhere in a camera roll there's a screenshot kept as proof: the unfair message, the thing someone said, saved for a reckoning that never quite comes.
Now a day the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, remembered as one of the hardest of his life. Tradition places it after the town of Ta'if turned him away.
He walks off, overwhelmed with grief, and doesn't come back to himself until he's far down the road. He looks up. A cloud is shading him, and in it is the angel Gabriel.
And Gabriel has brought someone with an offer.

teach.b: It's the angel of the mountains.
In the hadith in Bukhari, he greets the Prophet and says: if you wish, I will bring the two mountains together on them. One word, and the people who turned him away are gone. He says no.

He says he hopes that from their children, God will bring people who worship God alone. His wife Aisha said, in another report, that he never took revenge for his own sake. So how does that sit with today's Name?
Al-Muntaqim, the Requiter. The Qur'an calls Allah, in Pickthall's words, "Mighty, Able to Requite (the wrong)."

teach.h: AN ATOM'S WEIGHT WILL BE SEEN.
teach.b: And it promises: "And whoso doeth good an atom's weight will see it then, And whoso doeth ill an atom's weight will see it then." Here's the turn.
Because no wrong is forgotten by God, the Prophet didn't have to bring the mountains down himself.
The reckoning was held somewhere safer than his own anger, which left his hands free to hope for those people's children.
That's the line to tell a friend tonight: in this story, the one who was wronged is offered revenge, and spends the offer on his enemies' future. Al-Muntaqim isn't a God who loses His temper.
It's the promise that nothing done in the dark just disappears.

how: When wronged, some Muslims say hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakil, Allah is enough for us, still seeking fair redress while leaving the final reckoning to God.

o: the Recorder who writes down sins
the Requiter, who makes every wrong right
the Avenger who loses His temper

games.q: the offer on the road — tap the pairs.

s: Al-Muntaqim means God gets even the way an angry person does
the Name means nothing done is lost or left unanswered; it isn't a temper.
in the hadith, the Prophet turned down an angel's offer to destroy the people who turned him away
he hoped God would bring believers from their children instead.
leaving a wrong to God means pretending it never happened
the Qur'an says even an atom's weight of ill will be seen.

games.q: someone posts a cruel edited photo of your friend. your friend has a worse one ready to post back. what fits today's story?
o: post it; the Requiter wants every wrong answered, so answer it.
report the photo, skip the counter-post, leave the payback to God.
do nothing at all; even reporting it is a kind of revenge.
games.why: offered the mountains, the Prophet said no. fair steps are fine; the payback belongs to the One who forgets no wrong.

practice: On a scrap of paper, write a few words for one wrong you're still holding; no names needed. Fold it once and set it down beside you, out of your hand.
For the sit, let it stay there: not erased, not forgotten, just no longer yours alone to carry.

wordCard.voice: Al-Muntaqim. The Requiter, who makes right every wrong, so the one who was wronged doesn't have to carry the mountains.

orig.note: Arabic: the Requiter, from the traditional list of the Names; the Qur'an calls Allah 'Able to Requite (the wrong)'.

carryVoice: Hold on to this one: no wrong forgotten, not by Him, so your hands are free for something else. That's fifteen fifty-five.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 3231; Sahih Muslim 1795 (the angel of the mountains)
Sahih al-Bukhari 6126; Sahih Muslim 2328 (he never took revenge for his own sake)

sources.q: And whoso doeth good an atom's weight will see it then, And whoso doeth ill an atom's weight will see it then.
